h1: What Landscape Architects Look for in a Playground Equipment Manufacturer

props.title: What Landscape Architects Look for in a Playground Equipment Manufacturer
props.summaryText: What landscape architects need from a playground manufacturer to specify with confidence: drawings and data, design flexibility, safety information and a partner who delivers on site.
props.author: rohan-mehta
props.imageAlt: Children and adults in a green landscaped space with trees

takeaways.text: Architects need technical data early: dimensions, safety zones, fall heights, foundations and specifications.
Design flexibility matters: colours, materials and forms that suit the landscape, not just a catalogue.
The manufacturer should coordinate with the landscape contractor on levels, surfacing and drainage.
Reliable delivery and installation protect the architect's reputation on the project.

faq.q: What information should a playground manufacturer give an architect?
faq.a: Plan and elevation drawings, footprint and safety zone dimensions, free fall height, age range and user capacity, foundation details, material and finish specifications, colour options, and recommended surfacing for each unit.

faq.q: Can playground equipment be customised to match a landscape design?
faq.a: Often, yes. Colours, finishes and materials can usually be adapted, and some manufacturers create custom or nature-inspired designs. Ask early, because custom work affects cost and lead time.

faq.q: How should playground equipment be coordinated with landscaping?
faq.a: Agree finished levels, surfacing build-up, drainage, planting distances from safety zones, and the sequence of work between the landscape contractor and the playground installer before work starts on site.
